rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

examples: The earlier cards have said only that their eyes were opened. They have not mentioned nakedness or a need for coverings, so the baker cannot reason out “naked”; the blank tests unseen wording.

The setup quotes the general curse but gives no context from which the serpent's new movement can be inferred. “Belly” is therefore an unseen word the baker must guess rather than a meaning supported by the earlier cards.
Card 1 says only that Adam gives his wife a name. Nothing in the earlier cards allows the baker to reason out “Eve,” so this blank simply asks for an unseen name.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

examples: The phrase "that tree" points back to choice card 15, which the baker can no longer see. Make the question self-contained by identifying the forbidden tree.
“All of that” points back to the three descriptions on story card 9, which is no longer on screen. The question needs to supply the relevant context itself.
“After this” depends on the preceding story card, which is no longer visible. The question does not identify the statement or event that “this” refers to, so it is not self-contained.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

examples: The opening sentence retells the ground being watered from Genesis 2:6, but the card cites only Genesis 2:7. Include verse 6 in the citation or remove that recap.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

examples: Cards 2, 3, 4 and 9 all require facts not supplied by the earlier cards: Eve's name, the reason for that name, the material of the garments and what God stations at Eden. Only cards 7 and 10 offer a reasonable basis for an informed pick, so most of this stop's choices rely on guessing.

Three of the stop's five choice cards depend on discovery guesses rather than reasoning. Card 5 gives no indication of what Lamech will announce, card 6 gives three numbers that all satisfy the setup that Lamech “tops” sevenfold, and card 10 gives no basis for predicting what began in Enosh's days. Consequently, most of this stop's choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

examples: The wrong answers "Wait seven more days" and "Send out the dove again" describe actions that actually occur earlier in this passage: Noah waits seven more days and sends out the dove again in Genesis 8:10 and 8:12. They are therefore not false anywhere in the passage.

The wrong answer "Hold back the rain" is true elsewhere in the passage: Genesis 8:2 says that the rain from the sky was restrained. It cannot serve as a distractor under the false-anywhere-in-the-passage rule.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

examples: The wrong answer "still" is also defensible: God's work had already been called good, and the completed creation remains good. A baker could argue for it, leaving the card to hinge on the exact unseen adverb rather than a clearly false alternative.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both.

examples: The right answer "Multiply and fill the waters" is only true for the sea creatures. Genesis 1:22 tells the birds to multiply on the earth.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

examples: Genesis 8:13 places this event in Noah's six hundred and first year, but the card changes that into the definite statement that Noah was already six hundred and one years old. Those are not the same statement, and the added age is not supported by the text.

rule.text: A stretch never gets a stop of its own. Its one card sits in the stop with the moments around it.

examples: Genesis 10 is a long stretch, the list of nations, but it got a stop of its own with 4 story cards and 5 choice cards, most about Nimrod. It should be one story card in stop 1, with Nimrod as its standout detail and no choice cards.
